scientific_claim: Chemical filtering can enrich T relative to U through differential hydrolysis stability in dark hydrothermal-vent conditions. UV is negligible in this environment (zero-UV control differs by <2%). The model does not demonstrate Darwinian evolution. The CSI decomposes multiplicatively as CSI = real T-pref enrichment * pool-drift factor; the drift factor is a DERIVED RESIDUAL (drift = CSI / real), not an independently simulated mechanism. CSI is normalized by the INITIAL Miller-Orgel pool T-fraction (0.0661), not by the influx T-fraction (0.2727); csi_vs_influx and drift_independent are recorded as convention-free diagnostics. v6.6.1 HEADLINE RULE: quote dna_tu_over_influx and control_corrected_enrichment (see headline_metrics) alongside CSI, never CSI alone. Relative to the constant feedstock T/(U+T) = 0.2727, differential U hydrolysis raises DNA T/(U+T) from 0.67x (equal_degradation control, k_U = k_T) to 2.02x (baseline) at the v6.5.1 optimum: a ~3x control-corrected enrichment that is immune to the assumed influx stoichiometry and to the CSI normalization convention, because both arms of the decisive sweep share them. real = 0.887 compares DNA against the instantaneous free pool, which is itself the chemically filtered intermediate (free T/(U+T) rises 0.171 -> 0.620 vs feed 0.2727), so real < 1 is a lag, not a refutation. The result is conditional on the Arrhenius-extrapolated k_U/k_T ~ 357x rate ratio at 90 C and demonstrates chemical filtering, not Darwinian selection. v6.7.0 ADDS an opt-in sequence-resolved layer (SequenceEvolutionEngine, sequence_evolution_sweep) in which individuals are copolymeric 100-residue sequences that die on any chain-scission hit, reproduce Wright-Fisher style from survivors, and mutate with template-base-dependent copy errors; there the homopolymer and no-heredity caveats below do NOT apply, but its generation time and copy-error rates are assumed placeholders and its headline numbers are darwinian_gain and control_corrected_seq_enrichment in sequence_evolution_results. v6.7.0 reference values (10 seeds, 240 generations, pop 512, 90 C / pH 11): baseline population T/(U+T) 0.886 (3.25x feed); chemistry-only (no replication) goes EXTINCT in 10/10 seeds with a last-cohort T/(U+T) of 0.311; darwinian_gain 2.85; control_corrected_seq_enrichment 1.06, i.e. with the assumed copy-error rates the fidelity channel dominates the evolving-regime enrichment and the hydrolysis channel adds ~6%; no_mutation (heredity without variation) freezes as a clone at 0.393 - all three Darwinian components are required. The stability ratio k_U/k_T is an Arrhenius extrapolation, not a measurement; see the Ea_T sweep. The decisive_control_sweep tests whether the enrichment survives forcing k_U == k_T in (a) the polymer only, (b) the free pool only, and (c) both. The legacy UV module encodes T as LESS photoreactive than U, the OPPOSITE of the measured direction in Khosh Abady et al. (PNAS 2026); use uv_damage_mode='lesion_two_state' for the PNAS-informed two-state lesion model.

model_abstractions.homopolymer: Every 'DNA molecule' in VSSUFEngine is a homopolymer of 100 residues of one base; no sequence, no base pairing, no complementary strand; 'dsDNA' is a label only. v6.7.0 adds the opt-in SequenceEvolutionEngine (Section 6c), where individuals ARE copolymeric 100-residue sequences; the homopolymer caveat applies only to the VSSUFEngine results.
model_abstractions.csi_normalization: CSI = final DNA T-fraction / INITIAL-pool T-fraction (0.0661); influx T-fraction is 0.2727.
model_abstractions.drift_is_residual: pool_drift_factor = CSI / real by definition; see drift_independent for an independent diagnostic.
model_abstractions.uv_selectivity: legacy_irreversible mode: T cross-section 0.28x U (opposite of PNAS 2026). lesion_two_state mode: T hit rate 2.7x U (PNAS-informed), lesions split into reversible CPDs and lethal (6-4).
model_abstractions.free_monomer_hydrolysis: Free U/T hydrolysis rate = polymer rate * FREE_HYDRO_SCALE (assumed, default 1.0); placeholder for measured free-nucleotide kinetics.
model_abstractions.decomposed_destruction_channels: polymer hydrolysis and free-monomer hydrolysis are independently equalizable; equal_polymer_only and equal_free_only isolate the two channels; equal_degradation equalizes both.

known_limitations: Homopolymer abstraction (VSSUFEngine only): results describe populations of single-base 100-mers, not copolymeric genetic molecules. The opt-in v6.7.0 SequenceEvolutionEngine removes this for its own outputs but does not retroactively change the homopolymer results.
The k_U/k_T ~ 357x stability ratio is inherited almost entirely from the assumed 25 C reference-rate ratio (1.3e-10 / 1.1e-13 ~ 1182x) plus assumed Ea values; it is an input, not an output.
FREE_HYDRO_SCALE, CPD fractions, and PHOTOREVERSION_RATE are assumed placeholders; sweeps bound but do not measure their influence.
CSI magnitude depends on pool-composition conventions (initial pool vs influx); see the equal_pools control.

csi_vs_influx divides the DNA all-base T-fraction by the influx T/(U+T) fraction (mismatched denominators); use dna_tu_over_influx from headline_metrics for the consistent feedstock-relative comparison.
Influx stoichiometry INFLUX_T = 45 vs INFLUX_U = 120 residues/s is assumed; it fixes the influx T/(U+T) = 0.2727 that drives the drift term dominating CSI. See the influx_ratio_sweep.

No Darwinian evolution in VSSUFEngine: no replication with heredity or selection on fidelity. The opt-in v6.7.0 SequenceEvolutionEngine adds heredity, mutation, and differential survival, but its Wright-Fisher generation time (1 h), population cap (512), and per-position copy-error rates (0.01; 0.05 on U templates) are ASSUMED, and it models no base pairing, no complementary strand, and no specific copying chemistry.

optimization_results.horizon_note: peak CSI coincides with the simulation horizon; enrichment is still rising at the boundary (see time_horizon_sweep), so the optimum is a horizon artifact, not a peak
optimization_results.stability_ratio_label: extrapolated (25 C refs -> 90 C; Ea_T assumed 32 kcal/mol; see ea_T_sweep for uncertainty)

headline_metrics.interpretation: CSI is normalized by the INITIAL pool T-fraction (0.0661) and is dominated by the drift term; quote the feedstock-relative metrics instead. dna_tu_over_influx compares DNA T/(U+T) against the constant feed T/(U+T) with consistent denominators. control_corrected_enrichment divides that ratio by the same ratio under equal_degradation (k_U = k_T); both arms of the decisive sweep share every assumption, including the assumed influx stoichiometry, so the ratio is immune to them. v6.5.1 reference values: baseline 2.02x, equal_degradation 0.67x, control-corrected ~3.0x. real < 1 (DNA vs the instantaneous free pool) is a lag, not a refutation: the free pool is itself the filtered intermediate (free T/(U+T) 0.171 -> 0.620 vs feed 0.2727). Conditional on the Arrhenius-extrapolated k_U/k_T ~ 357x rate ratio at 90 C. Chemical filtering, not Darwinian selection.

decisive_control_sweep.decision_rule: Claim 'free-pool hydrolysis drives enrichment' is SUPPORTED if equal_polymer_only CSI ~ baseline CSI AND equal_free_only CSI ~ equal_degradation CSI (both within 95% CI). REFUTED if equal_polymer_only CSI drops substantially toward 1 OR equal_free_only CSI stays near baseline. MIXED otherwise.

horizon_edge_warning: The reported optimum has peak CSI at the simulation horizon (time_to_peak_csi_h = 239.8 h). Enrichment is still rising at the boundary; see time_horizon_sweep. Do not quote the horizon-edge value as a converged optimum.
